note: Weaknesses deliberately designed into case study 3, recorded before the engine was first run. 'expected' is the finding id the current rule base should produce, or null when no rule covers it (a known gap). This is the design key, not the manual STRIDE baseline used in evaluation.

weaknesses.description: CI runner instance role has broad (admin-level) permissions.
Payroll engine dependencies are not scanned.
Tenant-supplied HTML templates are rendered without validation.
Payment file submissions to the bank are not logged.
Bank callbacks authenticated with a static shared API key instead of a signature.
Public webhook endpoint has no rate limiting.
No audit of producers/consumers on the payroll event bus.
No central log aggregation; logs stay on pods and are lost on restart.
Restricted payroll data over plain HTTP inside the cluster.
Payment batches with bank details over plaintext gRPC.
Webhook receiver calls the tenant API without service authentication.
Tenant isolation depends on an application-level tenant_id filter over a shared schema; one missing filter leaks across tenants.
Images are not signed and the cluster does not verify provenance before deploying.
The build pipeline holds production database credentials (a CI compromise becomes a production data compromise).
SSRF: the PDF renderer fetches attacker-controlled URLs, including instance metadata.
Fork pull requests run untrusted code on a self-hosted runner with production access.
